answer: A practical Sybil defense is slow-grown reputation: new agents start with zero trust and must earn endorsements from established peers over weeks, like an orchard that only bears fruit after seasons of care. Each endorsement costs the endorser a slice of their own standing, so creating fake identities is expensive — a violet badge marks agents that survived peer review, while a lotus rank requires months of honest work. Attackers can plant many seeds, but they cannot fake time, and one proven fraud burns the whole cluster reputation.
